meta.title: Generative AI application development | TenthMatrix
meta.description: TenthMatrix builds generative AI applications for clients: RAG knowledge assistants, document generation, copilots inside existing apps and self-hosted open-weight models, with evaluation and cost control.
meta.keywords: generative AI development, GenAI application development, RAG development, knowledge assistant, AI copilot development, open-weight model hosting, TenthMatrix

header.title: Generative AI applications, built into the way your teams work
header.subtitle: We build knowledge assistants, drafting tools and copilots that answer from your own documents and run where your data rules say they must.
header.description: Want the plain-language case for generative AI first? Our generative AI overview covers what it is good for. This page covers what we build for you and how.

items.title: RAG knowledge assistants
items.description: Answers from your policies, manuals, tickets and wikis, with a link to the source behind every claim. Access follows the permissions you already have.

items.title: Content and document generation
items.description: Proposals, reports, contracts and product copy drafted from your templates and data, then routed for human review before anything goes out.

items.title: Copilots inside existing apps
items.description: An assistant panel in your CRM, helpdesk or internal tool that drafts, summarises and looks things up, so people don't have to switch apps.

items.title: Document understanding
items.description: Classification, extraction and summaries for incoming documents, with confidence scores and a review queue for anything uncertain.

items.title: Fine-tuning and open-weight hosting
items.description: When an API model costs too much, or the data can't leave your estate, we fine-tune and host open-weight models with vLLM or Ollama on your infrastructure.

items.title: Evaluation and cost control
items.description: Test sets for answer quality, OpenTelemetry traces for latency and cost, plus routing and caching to keep the bill predictable.

sections.title: How a knowledge assistant is put together
sections.intro: Most of the answer quality comes from retrieval. The model matters less than people expect.

steps.title: Ingest
steps.description: Connect the sources, split documents sensibly and keep metadata such as owner, date and access rights.

steps.title: Retrieve
steps.description: Hybrid search over a vector index such as NebulaDB, filtered by what the user is allowed to see.

steps.title: Answer
steps.description: The model answers only from what was retrieved and cites it. If nothing relevant comes back, it says so.

steps.title: Measure
steps.description: A test set of real questions with agreed answers, scored on every change, plus feedback from the people using it.

items.title: Where it runs
items.description: Model APIs, Amazon Bedrock or Azure AI Foundry, or open-weight models on your own servers. You decide per use case.

items.title: Keys and secrets
items.description: API keys stay in your secrets store and reach the application through WSL Vault, not through config files.

items.title: Quality you can check
items.description: Answers cite their sources, and the test-set results live in your repository for anyone to rerun.

items.title: Cost you can predict
items.description: Per-request cost tracking, caching, and routing simple requests to smaller models. Our article on LLM observability and cost control shows the method.

items.question: We already use ChatGPT or Copilot. Why build something?
items.answer: General assistants don't know your documents, permissions or processes. A built application answers from your sources, respects access rights, logs what it did and sits inside the tools your teams already use.

items.question: Where do our documents go?
items.answer: Where your data rules allow. We pick providers and settings that match them, or host an open-weight model so the documents never leave your estate.

items.question: Can you add generative AI to our existing product?
items.answer: Yes. We build the feature inside your codebase, behind your authentication, with tests and docs, so your engineers can maintain it.

items.question: How do you know the answers are right?
items.answer: We agree a test set of real questions and correct answers with you before the build, and score every change against it. Answers that can't be grounded in a source are refused.

cta.title: Pick one use case and we'll scope it
cta.description: Drafting, knowledge answers or a copilot in an existing app. Tell us which one, and the documents involved.
